entities.name: Little penguin
entities.fact: The little penguin stands only about 30 centimetres tall and breeds along the southern coasts of Australia, including Phillip Island.

entities.name: Australian fur seal
entities.fact: The Australian fur seal breeds on rocky islands in Bass Strait, between the Australian mainland and Tasmania.

entities.name: Eastern blue groper
entities.fact: The eastern blue groper is the state fish of New South Wales and is protected from fishing there.

entities.name: Australian salmon
entities.fact: Despite its name, the Australian salmon is not a true salmon but a schooling fish of the southern Australian coast.

entities.name: Yellow-eyed penguin
entities.fact: The yellow-eyed penguin, or hoiho, is among the rarest penguins and breeds on New Zealand's south-eastern coasts and subantarctic islands.

entities.name: New Zealand fur seal
entities.fact: The New Zealand fur seal, or kekeno, was hunted almost to extinction in the nineteenth century but has since recovered around New Zealand's coasts.

entities.name: Australasian snapper
entities.fact: The Australasian snapper, simply called snapper in New Zealand, is a pinkish sea bream that is one of the most popular fish there to catch and eat.

entities.name: Northern royal albatross
entities.fact: Taiaroa Head near Dunedin hosts the only mainland breeding colony of royal albatrosses in the world.

entities.name: Australasian gannet
entities.fact: Australasian gannets breed in large colonies such as the one at Cape Kidnappers on New Zealand's North Island.

entities.name: Tarakihi
entities.fact: Tarakihi is a silvery, banded fish of New Zealand's coastal waters and one of the country's most commonly eaten fish.

entities.name: Hapuku
entities.fact: The hapuku, or groper, is a large deep-water fish of New Zealand's rocky reefs and continental slope.

entities.name: Fiordland crested penguin
entities.fact: The Fiordland crested penguin, or tawaki, nests under the temperate rainforest of Fiordland and Stewart Island.

entities.name: Saddle wrasse
entities.fact: The saddle wrasse is a colourful fish found only in the Hawaiian Islands and nearby Johnston Atoll, and it is one of the most common fish on Hawaiian reefs.

entities.name: Hawaiian bobtail squid
entities.fact: The Hawaiian bobtail squid hosts glowing bacteria in a special organ that lets it hide its shadow from predators on moonlit nights.

entities.name: Green anaconda
entities.fact: The green anaconda is the heaviest snake in the world and spends most of its life in or beside slow water in the Amazon basin.

entities.name: Caiman
entities.fact: Caimans are South and Central American crocodilians that are close relatives of alligators.

entities.name: Capybara
entities.fact: The capybara is the largest living rodent and is a strong swimmer that can stay submerged for several minutes.

entities.name: Giant otter
entities.fact: Giant otters live in noisy family groups and can reach nearly 1.8 metres in length, making them the longest otters.

entities.name: Black caiman
entities.fact: The black caiman is the largest predator of the Amazon basin and can grow to about 5 metres long.

entities.name: Amazonian manatee
entities.fact: The Amazonian manatee is the only manatee that lives entirely in fresh water.

entities.name: Red-bellied piranha
entities.fact: The red-bellied piranha hunts in shoals and uses razor-sharp, interlocking teeth to slice flesh from its prey.

entities.name: Tambaqui
entities.fact: The tambaqui follows the flooded forest in the wet season and cracks fallen fruits and nuts with its strong, flat teeth.

entities.name: Pacu
entities.fact: Pacu are relatives of piranhas with flat, human-like molars that they use to crush seeds and nuts.

entities.name: Spectacled caiman
entities.fact: The spectacled caiman is named for a bony ridge between its eyes that looks like the bridge of a pair of spectacles.

entities.name: Giant South American river turtle
entities.fact: The giant South American river turtle is the largest river turtle in the region, and females gather in large numbers to nest on sandbanks.

entities.name: Matamata
entities.fact: The matamata looks like a pile of bark and leaves on the river bed and gulps down fish by suddenly opening its mouth to create suction.

entities.name: Black piranha
entities.fact: The black piranha is among the largest piranhas and is a fierce predator of the Amazon and Orinoco basins.

entities.name: Trahira
entities.fact: The trahira is an ambush predator of South American rivers with strong jaws and large teeth.

entities.name: Yellow-spotted river turtle
entities.fact: The yellow-spotted river turtle is named for the bright yellow spots on the head of the young and of females.

entities.name: Rummy-nose tetra
entities.fact: The rummy-nose tetra has a bright red nose and swims in tight, synchronised shoals.

entities.name: Amazon leaffish
entities.fact: The Amazon leaffish drifts in the water like a dead leaf, then snaps up small fish that come close.

entities.name: Nile tilapia
entities.fact: The Nile tilapia is a mouthbrooding fish native to Africa and is now one of the most widely farmed freshwater fish in the world.

entities.name: Mozambique tilapia
entities.fact: The Mozambique tilapia can tolerate salt water as well as fresh, which has helped it spread to rivers and coasts around the world.

entities.name: Freshwater butterflyfish
entities.fact: The freshwater butterflyfish lurks at the surface of West and Central African waters with its large fins spread like wings, and can leap clear of the water.

entities.name: Electric yellow cichlid
entities.fact: The electric yellow cichlid is a bright yellow mouthbrooder found only in Lake Malawi.

entities.name: Mbuna
entities.fact: Mbuna are the colourful, rock-dwelling cichlids of Lake Malawi, a lake that holds hundreds of cichlid species.

entities.name: Tropheus
entities.fact: Tropheus are rock-dwelling cichlids of Lake Tanganyika that come in a remarkable variety of colour forms.

entities.name: Frontosa
entities.fact: The frontosa is a large, banded cichlid of the deep water of Lake Tanganyika, and older males develop a prominent bump on the forehead.

entities.name: Peacock cichlid
entities.fact: Male peacock cichlids of Lake Malawi flash vivid blue and gold colours as they court females over sandy lake floors.

entities.name: Yellowfish
entities.fact: Yellowfish are large minnow relatives of southern African rivers that are prized by fly anglers.

entities.name: Vundu
entities.fact: The vundu is a large catfish of central and southern African rivers such as the Zambezi, and it can grow well over a metre long.

entities.name: African pike
entities.fact: The African pike is a fast, toothy predator of African rivers that guards its nest of foam-bubbles.

entities.name: Chambo
entities.fact: Chambo is the name given to a group of tilapia from Lake Malawi, which are among the favourite food fish in Malawi.

entities.name: Kapenta
entities.fact: Kapenta are tiny sardine-like fish from Lake Tanganyika that were introduced to Lake Kariba in the 1960s, where they now support a large fishery.

entities.name: Congo tetra
entities.fact: Male Congo tetras of the Congo basin shimmer with rainbow colours and have long, flowing fins.

entities.name: Julidochromis
entities.fact: Julidochromis are small, striped cichlids that live and breed in rocky crevices in Lake Tanganyika.

entities.name: Shell-dwelling cichlid
entities.fact: This tiny cichlid of Lake Tanganyika lives in empty snail shells on the lake bed and defends a territory of shells like a miniature colony.

entities.name: African knifefish
entities.fact: The African knifefish swims by rippling a long fin along its belly and can breathe air at the surface.

entities.name: Ornate bichir
entities.fact: The ornate bichir is a primitive-looking African fish that has lungs and can gulp air at the surface.

entities.name: Turquoise killifish
entities.fact: The turquoise killifish lives in seasonal pools in Zimbabwe and Mozambique, and its eggs survive the dry season buried in mud.

entities.name: Aba aba
entities.fact: The aba aba swims forwards and backwards with equal ease and senses its surroundings with a weak electric field.

entities.name: African arowana
entities.fact: The African arowana is a large, air-gulping fish of West and Central African rivers and floodplains.

entities.name: Kampango
entities.fact: The kampango is a large catfish of Lake Malawi and its rivers.

entities.name: Dagaa
entities.fact: Dagaa are tiny silver fish of Lake Victoria that are dried in the sun and eaten across East Africa.

entities.name: Fahaka puffer
entities.fact: The fahaka puffer lives in the Nile and other African rivers and can inflate its body with water when threatened.

entities.name: African moony
entities.fact: The African moony is a silvery, disc-shaped fish of West African estuaries and rivers that can live in fresh or brackish water.

entities.name: Magadi tilapia
entities.fact: The Magadi tilapia lives in hot, caustic soda lagoons beside Kenya's Lake Magadi, where the water can exceed 35 degrees Celsius and is highly alkaline.

entities.name: Jamaica
entities.fact: Jamaica is the third-largest island of the Greater Antilles and the birthplace of reggae music.

entities.name: Barbados
entities.fact: Barbados is the most easterly of the Caribbean islands and is built largely of coral limestone rather than volcanic rock.

entities.name: Aruba
entities.fact: Aruba lies about 29 kilometres off the coast of Venezuela and is one of the Dutch Caribbean's ABC islands.

entities.name: Hispaniola
entities.fact: Hispaniola is shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic and is the second-largest island in the Caribbean.

entities.name: Trinidad
entities.fact: Trinidad is the larger island of Trinidad and Tobago and lies only about 11 kilometres off the coast of Venezuela.

entities.name: Saint Lucia
entities.fact: Saint Lucia's twin volcanic peaks, the Pitons, rise straight out of the sea and are a World Heritage Site.

entities.name: Curaçao
entities.fact: Curaçao is the largest of the Dutch ABC islands, and the old harbour of its capital Willemstad is a World Heritage Site.

entities.name: Antigua
entities.fact: Antigua is home to Nelson's Dockyard, an eighteenth-century Royal Navy base that is a World Heritage Site.

entities.name: Grenada
entities.fact: Grenada is nicknamed the Spice Isle for the nutmeg and mace it grows and exports.

entities.name: Martinique
entities.fact: Martinique is a French island where the eruption of Mont Pelée destroyed the town of Saint-Pierre in 1902.

entities.name: Guadeloupe
entities.fact: Guadeloupe is shaped like a butterfly, with two main islands, Basse-Terre and Grande-Terre, split by a narrow channel.

entities.name: Dominica
entities.fact: Dominica, the Nature Isle, is a rugged volcanic island with a flooded fumarole known as the Boiling Lake.

entities.name: Saint Kitts
entities.fact: Saint Kitts is the larger island of Saint Kitts and Nevis, the smallest country in the Americas by area.

entities.name: Saint Vincent
entities.fact: Saint Vincent is a volcanic island where the La Soufrière volcano erupted in 2021.

entities.name: Tobago
entities.fact: Tobago is the smaller island of Trinidad and Tobago and is known for the coral gardens of Buccoo Reef.

entities.name: Bonaire
entities.fact: Bonaire is famed for shore diving, and its coastal waters have been a marine park since 1979.

entities.name: Saint Martin
entities.fact: The island of Saint Martin is divided between France and the Netherlands, who have shared it since a treaty in 1648.

entities.name: Saint Thomas
entities.fact: Saint Thomas is one of the US Virgin Islands and its capital, Charlotte Amalie, is a busy cruise port.

entities.name: Cayman Islands
entities.fact: The Cayman Islands are made up of Grand Cayman, Little Cayman and Cayman Brac, which rise steeply from very deep water south of Cuba.

entities.name: Cozumel
entities.fact: Cozumel lies off Mexico's Yucatán coast and is known for drift diving along the Mesoamerican Reef.

entities.name: Roatán
entities.fact: Roatán is the largest of Honduras's Bay Islands and lies beside the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef.

entities.name: Isla Margarita
entities.fact: Isla Margarita is Venezuela's largest island and was a centre of pearl fishing in the sixteenth century.

entities.name: Tortola
entities.fact: Tortola is the largest of the British Virgin Islands.

entities.name: Saint Croix
entities.fact: Saint Croix is the largest of the US Virgin Islands and was once a Danish sugar colony.

entities.name: Saint John
entities.fact: Much of Saint John in the US Virgin Islands is protected as the Virgin Islands National Park.

entities.name: Anguilla
entities.fact: Anguilla is a long, thin, flat coral island whose name is generally said to come from the word for eel.

entities.name: Montserrat
entities.fact: Montserrat is called the Emerald Isle of the Caribbean, and its Soufrière Hills volcano buried the capital, Plymouth, in the 1990s.

entities.name: Nevis
entities.fact: Nevis is a round volcanic island whose peak is often wreathed in cloud, and Alexander Hamilton was born there.

entities.name: Saba
entities.fact: Saba is a tiny Dutch island that is the top of a single volcano, Mount Scenery, the highest point in the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

entities.name: Sint Eustatius
entities.fact: Sint Eustatius, known as Statia, was a busy trading port in the eighteenth century and is dominated by the Quill volcano.

entities.name: Saint Barthélemy
entities.fact: Saint Barthélemy is a small French island that belonged to Sweden from 1784 to 1878.

entities.name: Bequia
entities.fact: Bequia is the largest of the Grenadines that belong to Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and is known for traditional wooden boat-building.

entities.name: Mustique
entities.fact: Mustique is a small privately owned island in the Grenadines that is popular with celebrities.

entities.name: Carriacou
entities.fact: Carriacou is the largest of the Grenadine islands and is known for its boat-building tradition.

entities.name: Virgin Gorda
entities.fact: Virgin Gorda is home to the Baths, a beach of giant granite boulders that form sea-filled grottoes.

entities.name: Jost Van Dyke
entities.fact: Jost Van Dyke is a small British Virgin Island famed for its beach bars, such as the Soggy Dollar Bar.

entities.name: Anegada
entities.fact: Anegada is a flat coral island, unlike the other volcanic British Virgin Islands, and is ringed by Horseshoe Reef, where many ships have wrecked.

entities.name: Barbuda
entities.fact: Barbuda is the smaller island of Antigua and Barbuda and has a large frigatebird colony at Codrington Lagoon.

entities.name: Vieques
entities.fact: Vieques, off Puerto Rico, is home to Mosquito Bay, whose water glows with bioluminescent plankton.

entities.name: Culebra
entities.fact: Culebra is a small Puerto Rican island with Flamenco Beach and a national wildlife refuge.

entities.name: Mona Island
entities.fact: Mona Island lies in the Mona Passage between Puerto Rico and Hispaniola and is a nature reserve with giant Mona iguanas.

entities.name: Isla de la Juventud
entities.fact: The Isla de la Juventud is Cuba's largest offshore island and was once called the Isle of Pines.

entities.name: San Andrés
entities.fact: San Andrés is a Colombian island that lies far closer to Nicaragua than to the Colombian mainland.

entities.name: Providencia
entities.fact: Providencia is a small volcanic Colombian island in the western Caribbean that was once used as a base by the pirate Henry Morgan.

entities.name: Utila
entities.fact: Utila is one of Honduras's Bay Islands and is a popular place to learn to dive, with occasional whale shark sightings.

entities.name: Guanaja
entities.fact: Guanaja is the easternmost of Honduras's Bay Islands and was visited by Christopher Columbus in 1502.

entities.name: Little Cayman
entities.fact: Little Cayman is the smallest of the three Cayman Islands and has very few residents.

entities.name: Cayman Brac
entities.fact: Cayman Brac is named after its bluff, which rises about 43 metres, as 'brac' is the Gaelic word for bluff.

entities.name: Union Island
entities.fact: Union Island is one of the Grenadines and a hub for sailors, with its main port at Clifton.

entities.name: Mayreau
entities.fact: Mayreau is a tiny Grenadine island with no airport and only a few hundred residents.

entities.name: Marie-Galante
entities.fact: Marie-Galante is a round island of Guadeloupe that was once covered in sugar mills and is known for its rum.

entities.name: La Désirade
entities.fact: La Désirade, a dry narrow island east of Guadeloupe, was the first land Columbus sighted on his second voyage in 1493.

entities.name: Les Saintes
entities.fact: Les Saintes are a cluster of small islands south of Guadeloupe, where the Battle of the Saintes was fought in 1782.

entities.name: Navassa Island
entities.fact: Navassa Island is an uninhabited Caribbean island between Jamaica and Haiti that is administered by the United States and claimed by Haiti.

entities.name: Madagascar
entities.fact: Madagascar is the fourth-largest island in the world, and every species of lemur lives only there.

entities.name: Sri Lanka
entities.fact: Sri Lanka is a teardrop-shaped island off the southern tip of India, separated from it by the Palk Strait.

entities.name: Mauritius
entities.fact: Mauritius was the only home of the dodo, a flightless bird that was extinct by the late seventeenth century.

entities.name: Bali
entities.fact: Bali is a mainly Hindu island in Indonesia, a country with a Muslim majority, and lies just east of Java.

entities.name: Maldives
entities.fact: The Maldives are about a thousand coral islands grouped into atolls, and the country is the lowest-lying on Earth.

entities.name: Zanzibar
entities.fact: Zanzibar lies off the coast of Tanzania and was once a centre of the spice and slave trades.

entities.name: Réunion
entities.fact: Réunion is a French island whose volcano, the Piton de la Fournaise, is one of the most active in the world.

entities.name: Java
entities.fact: Java is the most populous island in the world and is home to Jakarta, the capital of Indonesia.

entities.name: Sumatra
entities.fact: Sumatra is the sixth-largest island in the world and is home to wild orangutans, tigers, rhinos and elephants.

entities.name: Mahé
entities.fact: Mahé is the largest island of the Seychelles and is home to its capital, Victoria.

entities.name: Lombok
entities.fact: Lombok lies just east of Bali across the Lombok Strait and is dominated by the volcano Mount Rinjani.

entities.name: Komodo
entities.fact: Komodo is the Indonesian island that gave its name to the Komodo dragon, the largest living lizard.

entities.name: Phuket
entities.fact: Phuket is Thailand's largest island and lies in the Andaman Sea.

entities.name: Socotra
entities.fact: Socotra lies off the Horn of Africa and more than a third of its plant species grow nowhere else, including the dragon's blood tree.

entities.name: Diego Garcia
entities.fact: Diego Garcia is the largest island of the Chagos Archipelago and hosts a joint United States and British military base.

entities.name: Christmas Island
entities.fact: Christmas Island, an Australian territory in the Indian Ocean, is famous for the annual migration of millions of red crabs.

entities.name: Langkawi
entities.fact: Langkawi is an archipelago of about 100 islands in the Andaman Sea off the north-west coast of Malaysia.

entities.name: Penang
entities.fact: Penang is an island off the north-west coast of Malaysia, and its capital, George Town, is a World Heritage Site.

entities.name: Andaman Islands
entities.fact: The Andaman Islands are an Indian archipelago in the Bay of Bengal, and on North Sentinel Island people live in isolation from the outside world.

entities.name: Praslin
entities.fact: Praslin in the Seychelles is home to the Vallée de Mai, where the coco de mer, the largest seed in the world, grows.

entities.name: La Digue
entities.fact: La Digue in the Seychelles is a small island where bicycles and ox carts are still common, and it is known for its granite boulder beaches.

entities.name: Grande Comore
entities.fact: Grande Comore is the largest island of the Comoros and is dominated by the active volcano Mount Karthala.

entities.name: Mayotte
entities.fact: Mayotte is a French island in the Comoros archipelago that is encircled by a large coral lagoon.

entities.name: Rodrigues
entities.fact: Rodrigues is a small volcanic island that is part of Mauritius, about 560 kilometres east of the main island.

entities.name: Nosy Be
entities.fact: Nosy Be is an island off north-west Madagascar known for its ylang-ylang perfume plantations.

entities.name: Pemba Island
entities.fact: Pemba Island lies north of Zanzibar off the coast of Tanzania and is known for its cloves.

entities.name: Lamu
entities.fact: Lamu is a Kenyan island with a World Heritage old Swahili town where there are almost no cars and donkeys carry goods.

entities.name: Mafia Island
entities.fact: Mafia Island, off Tanzania, has a marine park where whale sharks gather in season.

entities.name: Cocos Islands
entities.fact: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands are two Australian atolls in the Indian Ocean that Charles Darwin visited in 1836 while developing his ideas on atoll formation.

entities.name: Nicobar Islands
entities.fact: The Nicobar Islands are an Indian chain lying south of the Andaman Islands, not far from the northern tip of Sumatra.

entities.name: Nias
entities.fact: Nias is an Indonesian island off the west coast of Sumatra that is known for its world-class surf breaks.

entities.name: Flores
entities.fact: Flores is an Indonesian island where the remains of the small extinct human Homo floresiensis, nicknamed the hobbit, were found.

entities.name: Sumba
entities.fact: Sumba is an Indonesian island known for its megalithic tombs and its hand-woven ikat textiles.

entities.name: Kerguelen Islands
entities.fact: The Kerguelen Islands are a remote French sub-Antarctic archipelago in the southern Indian Ocean, sometimes called the Desolation Islands.

entities.name: Rottnest Island
entities.fact: Rottnest Island, off Perth in Western Australia, is home to the quokka, a small marsupial that appears to smile.

entities.name: Heard Island
entities.fact: Heard Island is a glaciated Australian sub-Antarctic island with an active volcano, Big Ben, the highest mountain in Australian territory.

entities.name: Crozet Islands
entities.fact: The Crozet Islands are a French sub-Antarctic archipelago famed for their huge colonies of king penguins.

entities.name: Amsterdam Island
entities.fact: Amsterdam Island is a remote French volcanic island in the southern Indian Ocean and the only home of the Amsterdam albatross.

entities.name: Marion Island
entities.fact: Marion Island is a South African sub-Antarctic island with a weather station and large colonies of seabirds and seals.

entities.name: Bazaruto
entities.fact: Bazaruto is an island archipelago off Mozambique that is a national park and a refuge for dugongs.

entities.name: Ibo Island
entities.fact: Ibo Island lies in Mozambique's Quirimbas Archipelago and has an old Portuguese fort and a tradition of silverwork.

entities.name: Sainte-Marie
entities.fact: Sainte-Marie, off eastern Madagascar, was a pirate base in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, and humpback whales gather there each year.

entities.name: Silhouette Island
entities.fact: Silhouette Island is a mountainous island in the Seychelles, most of which is a national park.

entities.name: Siberut
entities.fact: Siberut is the largest of the Mentawai Islands off Sumatra and is home to several primates found nowhere else.

entities.name: Simeulue
entities.fact: Simeulue is an Indonesian island off Sumatra where the local oral tradition of fleeing to high ground after an earthquake saved many lives in the 2004 tsunami.

entities.name: Lakshadweep
entities.fact: Lakshadweep is an Indian archipelago of coral islands in the Arabian Sea off the coast of Kerala.

entities.name: Masirah Island
entities.fact: Masirah is an Omani island that hosts one of the largest nesting populations of loggerhead turtles in the world.

entities.name: Dirk Hartog Island
entities.fact: Dirk Hartog Island off Western Australia is where the Dutch captain Dirk Hartog left a pewter plate in 1616, the first known European landing on Australia's west coast.

entities.name: Mohéli
entities.fact: Mohéli is the smallest of the Comoros islands and has a marine park where green turtles nest.

entities.name: Anjouan
entities.fact: Anjouan is a volcanic island of the Comoros that is steep and green and is known for growing ylang-ylang.

entities.name: Frégate Island
entities.fact: Frégate Island in the Seychelles helped to save the Seychelles magpie-robin from extinction.

entities.name: Europa Island
entities.fact: Europa Island is an uninhabited French island in the Mozambique Channel where green turtles come to nest.

entities.name: Tromelin Island
entities.fact: Tromelin is a tiny, flat island east of Madagascar where enslaved people were abandoned in 1761 and the few survivors were rescued about fifteen years later.

entities.name: Sicily
entities.fact: Sicily is the largest island in the Mediterranean and is home to Mount Etna, one of the most active volcanoes in the world.

entities.name: Crete
entities.fact: Crete is the largest Greek island and the birthplace of the Minoan civilisation.

entities.name: Malta
entities.fact: Malta's prehistoric stone temples are older than both Stonehenge and the pyramids of Egypt.

entities.name: Cyprus
entities.fact: Cyprus is the third-largest island in the Mediterranean and, in Greek myth, the birthplace of the goddess Aphrodite.

entities.name: Mallorca
entities.fact: Mallorca is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands, and its Serra de Tramuntana mountains are a World Heritage Site.

entities.name: Sardinia
entities.fact: Sardinia is the second-largest island in the Mediterranean and is dotted with prehistoric stone towers called nuraghi.

entities.name: Corsica
entities.fact: Corsica is a mountainous French island and the birthplace of Napoleon Bonaparte, who was born in Ajaccio in 1769.

entities.name: Ibiza
entities.fact: Ibiza is a Balearic island famed for its clubs, and its old walled town, Dalt Vila, is a World Heritage Site.

entities.name: Santorini
entities.fact: Santorini is a crescent of islands around a flooded volcanic crater left by a huge eruption in the Bronze Age.

entities.name: Mykonos
entities.fact: Mykonos is a Cycladic island famous for its whitewashed windmills and lively nightlife.

entities.name: Rhodes
entities.fact: Rhodes was home to the Colossus of Rhodes, a giant bronze statue counted among the Seven Wonders of the ancient world.

entities.name: Corfu
entities.fact: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea whose old town is a World Heritage Site and which was long ruled by Venice.

entities.name: Menorca
entities.fact: Menorca is the quieter, easternmost island of the Balearics and is a UNESCO biosphere reserve.

entities.name: Elba
entities.fact: Elba is the Italian island where Napoleon was first exiled in 1814.

entities.name: Capri
entities.fact: Capri lies off the Bay of Naples and is known for its Blue Grotto, a sea cave lit by an eerie blue glow.

entities.name: Gozo
entities.fact: Gozo is the smaller sister island of Malta and has the Ġgantija temples, built around 3600 BC.

entities.name: Zakynthos
entities.fact: Zakynthos is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea whose beaches are nesting grounds for loggerhead turtles.

entities.name: Kefalonia
entities.fact: Kefalonia is the largest of the Greek Ionian Islands and the setting of the novel Captain Corelli's Mandolin.

entities.name: Naxos
entities.fact: Naxos is the largest island of the Cyclades and has the Portara, a huge marble doorway left from an unfinished temple.

entities.name: Kos
entities.fact: Kos is the Greek island traditionally regarded as the birthplace of Hippocrates, the father of medicine.

entities.name: Lesbos
entities.fact: Lesbos is the third-largest Greek island and the birthplace of the ancient poet Sappho.

entities.name: Formentera
entities.fact: Formentera is the smallest inhabited island of the Balearics and is reached by ferry from Ibiza.

entities.name: Paros
entities.fact: Paros is a Cycladic island whose fine white marble was used to carve the Venus de Milo.

entities.name: Milos
entities.fact: Milos is the Greek island where the famous statue of Venus de Milo was found in 1820.

entities.name: Hydra
entities.fact: Hydra is a Greek island in the Saronic Gulf where cars are largely banned and donkeys and boats are the main transport.

entities.name: Aegina
entities.fact: Aegina is a Greek island in the Saronic Gulf known for its pistachios and the ancient Temple of Aphaia.

entities.name: Patmos
entities.fact: Patmos is the Greek island where, by tradition, Saint John wrote the Book of Revelation.

entities.name: Ithaca
entities.fact: Ithaca is the Ionian island usually identified as the home of Odysseus in Homer's epic.

entities.name: Lefkada
entities.fact: Lefkada is a Greek Ionian island joined to the mainland by a causeway and a short floating bridge.

entities.name: Ischia
entities.fact: Ischia is a volcanic island in the Bay of Naples that is famous for its thermal springs.

entities.name: Lampedusa
entities.fact: Lampedusa is Italy's southernmost island and lies closer to Tunisia than to Sicily.

entities.name: Pantelleria
entities.fact: Pantelleria is a volcanic island between Sicily and Tunisia known for its sweet wine and its vines trained in sunken hollows.

entities.name: Hvar
entities.fact: Hvar is a Croatian island in the Adriatic Sea known for its lavender fields and sunshine.

entities.name: Korčula
entities.fact: Korčula is a Croatian island whose walled old town is claimed as the birthplace of the explorer Marco Polo.

entities.name: Djerba
entities.fact: Djerba is a Tunisian island joined to the mainland by a causeway and is traditionally identified with Homer's land of the Lotus-eaters.

entities.name: Brač
entities.fact: Brač is a Croatian island whose white limestone was used in building the White House in Washington.

entities.name: Krk
entities.fact: Krk is one of the two largest islands in the Adriatic Sea and is joined to the Croatian mainland by a bridge.

entities.name: Vis
entities.fact: Vis was closed to foreign visitors as a Yugoslav military base until 1989.

entities.name: Mljet
entities.fact: Mljet is a Croatian island whose western end is a national park with two saltwater lakes.

entities.name: Stromboli
entities.fact: Stromboli is a volcanic island of the Aeolian chain whose volcano has erupted almost continuously for centuries.

entities.name: Lipari
entities.fact: Lipari is the largest of the Aeolian Islands off the north coast of Sicily.

entities.name: Vulcano
entities.fact: Vulcano is an Aeolian island whose name gave us the word volcano.

entities.name: Favignana
entities.fact: Favignana is the largest of the Aegadian Islands off western Sicily and was long known for its tuna fishery.

entities.name: Ustica
entities.fact: Ustica is a volcanic island north of Sicily with Italy's first marine reserve, created in 1986.

entities.name: La Maddalena
entities.fact: La Maddalena is the main island of an archipelago national park off the north coast of Sardinia.

entities.name: Giglio
entities.fact: Giglio is a small Italian island off Tuscany where the cruise ship Costa Concordia capsized in 2012.

entities.name: Montecristo
entities.fact: Montecristo is a small Italian island that gave its name to Alexandre Dumas's novel The Count of Monte Cristo.

entities.name: Ponza
entities.fact: Ponza is the largest of the Pontine Islands, which lie off the Italian coast between Rome and Naples.

entities.name: Thasos
entities.fact: Thasos is a Greek island in the northern Aegean that was famed in antiquity for its marble and gold.

entities.name: Samothrace
entities.fact: Samothrace is the Greek island where the statue known as the Winged Victory was found in 1863.

entities.name: Chios
entities.fact: Chios is the only place in the world that produces mastic gum, taken from the resin of a local tree.

entities.name: Samos
entities.fact: Samos is the Greek island where the mathematician Pythagoras was born.

entities.name: Lemnos
entities.fact: Lemnos is a northern Aegean island whose harbour at Moudros was a key Allied base in the Gallipoli campaign.

entities.name: Karpathos
entities.fact: Karpathos is a long, rugged Greek island between Crete and Rhodes known for its traditional mountain villages.

entities.name: Kastellorizo
entities.fact: Kastellorizo is Greece's easternmost inhabited island and lies just off the Turkish coast.

entities.name: Gavdos
entities.fact: Gavdos, south of Crete, is the southernmost point of Greece and of Europe.

entities.name: United States
entities.fact: The United States has both Atlantic and Pacific coastlines, and Alaska and Hawaii extend its waters far into the northern and central Pacific.

entities.name: Brazil
entities.fact: Brazil has an Atlantic coastline of roughly 7,500 kilometres, and the mighty Amazon river empties into the ocean there.

entities.name: United Kingdom
entities.fact: The United Kingdom is made up of Great Britain, Northern Ireland and many smaller islands, and its western shores face the open Atlantic.

entities.name: Spain
entities.fact: Spain has Atlantic coastlines in Galicia and around Cádiz as well as a long Mediterranean coast.

entities.name: Portugal
entities.fact: The whole of mainland Portugal's coast faces the Atlantic, and its sailors launched the Age of Discovery from there.

entities.name: Canada
entities.fact: Canada has coastlines on the Atlantic, Pacific and Arctic oceans, giving it the longest coastline of any country.

entities.name: South Africa
entities.fact: South Africa has both an Atlantic coast, on the west, and an Indian Ocean coast, on the east, and the two oceans meet near Cape Agulhas.

entities.name: Morocco
entities.fact: Morocco has coasts on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Mediterranean Sea, and sits just across the Strait of Gibraltar from Spain.

entities.name: France
entities.fact: France has an Atlantic coast running from Brittany to the Spanish border as well as a Mediterranean coast.

entities.name: Argentina
entities.fact: Argentina's Atlantic coast runs for thousands of kilometres from the Río de la Plata south to Tierra del Fuego.

entities.name: Norway
entities.fact: Norway's coast is cut by deep fjords and faces the North Atlantic and the Norwegian Sea.

entities.name: Uruguay
entities.fact: Uruguay's coast runs from the Río de la Plata estuary out to the open Atlantic at the resort of Punta del Este.

entities.name: Nigeria
entities.fact: Nigeria's southern coast lies on the Gulf of Guinea, an arm of the Atlantic, where the Niger river builds a huge delta.

entities.name: Ghana
entities.fact: Ghana's Atlantic coast on the Gulf of Guinea is lined with old trading forts, including Cape Coast Castle.

entities.name: Senegal
entities.fact: Senegal's capital, Dakar, sits on the Cap-Vert peninsula, the westernmost point of mainland Africa, on the Atlantic.

entities.name: Venezuela
entities.fact: Venezuela has a long coast on the Caribbean Sea and the Atlantic, where the Orinoco river forms a vast delta.

entities.name: Angola
entities.fact: Angola has a long Atlantic coastline, and its capital, Luanda, is a major port.

entities.name: Dominican Republic
entities.fact: The Dominican Republic shares the island of Hispaniola with Haiti and has Atlantic shores in the north and Caribbean shores in the south.

entities.name: Haiti
entities.fact: Haiti occupies the western third of Hispaniola, with coasts on both the Atlantic Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.

entities.name: Guyana
entities.fact: Guyana's low, flat Atlantic coast is where most of its people live, many of them below sea level.

entities.name: Suriname
entities.fact: Suriname lies on South America's Atlantic coast, and the old centre of its capital, Paramaribo, is a World Heritage Site.

entities.name: Mauritania
entities.fact: Mauritania's Atlantic coast includes the Banc d'Arguin National Park, where millions of migratory birds spend the winter.

entities.name: Gambia
entities.fact: The Gambia is a narrow country that follows the Gambia River inland from a short Atlantic coast.

entities.name: Guinea
entities.fact: Guinea's capital, Conakry, sits on the Atlantic coast, and the Niger, Senegal and Gambia rivers all rise in its highlands.

entities.name: Sierra Leone
entities.fact: Sierra Leone's capital, Freetown, stands on a large natural harbour on the Atlantic coast.

entities.name: Liberia
entities.fact: Liberia's capital, Monrovia, is an Atlantic port named after the US president James Monroe.

entities.name: Cameroon
entities.fact: Cameroon's Atlantic coast lies at the corner of the Gulf of Guinea, close to the volcano Mount Cameroon.

entities.name: Gabon
entities.fact: Gabon's Atlantic coast includes beaches where forest elephants and hippos sometimes walk beside the surf.

entities.name: Ivory Coast
entities.fact: Ivory Coast has a coast on the Gulf of Guinea, where Abidjan is one of West Africa's major ports.

entities.name: Trinidad and Tobago
entities.fact: Trinidad and Tobago is a twin-island nation whose eastern shores face the open Atlantic, only a few kilometres off Venezuela.

entities.name: Namibia
entities.fact: Namibia's Atlantic coast is the Skeleton Coast, where the Namib Desert meets the sea.

entities.name: Togo
entities.fact: Togo's coast on the Gulf of Guinea is only about 50 kilometres long.

entities.name: Benin
entities.fact: Benin has roughly 120 kilometres of coastline on the Gulf of Guinea.

entities.name: Equatorial Guinea
entities.fact: Equatorial Guinea has a mainland coast on the Atlantic and includes the island of Bioko in the Gulf of Guinea.

entities.name: Republic of the Congo
entities.fact: The Republic of the Congo has a short Atlantic coast around Pointe-Noire, its second city and main port.

entities.name: Guinea-Bissau
entities.fact: Guinea-Bissau's Atlantic coast includes the Bijagós Archipelago, which has more than 80 islands.

entities.name: Antigua and Barbuda
entities.fact: Antigua and Barbuda is a twin-island nation lying where the Atlantic Ocean meets the Caribbean Sea.

entities.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
entities.fact: The Democratic Republic of the Congo has only about 37 kilometres of Atlantic coast, at the mouth of the Congo River.

entities.name: China
entities.fact: China's eastern coast faces the Pacific through the Yellow, East China and South China seas.

entities.name: Australia
entities.fact: Australia has coastlines on both the Pacific and Indian oceans, and the Great Barrier Reef lies off its Pacific coast.

entities.name: Mexico
entities.fact: Mexico has a long Pacific coast, as well as coasts on the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean Sea.

entities.name: Russia
entities.fact: Russia's Pacific coast includes the port of Vladivostok and the volcanic Kamchatka Peninsula.

entities.name: Indonesia
entities.fact: Indonesia is an archipelago of about 17,000 islands with coasts on both the Pacific and Indian oceans.

entities.name: Chile
entities.fact: Chile is a ribbon of land about 4,300 kilometres long that has a Pacific coast along its entire western side.

entities.name: Peru
entities.fact: Peru's Pacific coast is washed by the cold Humboldt Current, which feeds one of the world's richest fisheries.

entities.name: Colombia
entities.fact: Colombia is the only South American country with coasts on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea.

entities.name: Ecuador
entities.fact: Ecuador is named after the equator, which crosses it, and it owns the Galápagos Islands in the Pacific.

entities.name: South Korea
entities.fact: South Korea has coasts on the Yellow Sea, the Korea Strait and the East Sea, which are all part of the Pacific.

entities.name: Vietnam
entities.fact: Vietnam has an S-shaped coastline of more than 3,000 kilometres on the South China Sea.

entities.name: Papua New Guinea
entities.fact: Papua New Guinea occupies the eastern half of the island of New Guinea and is bordered by the Pacific, and it has over 800 languages.

entities.name: Panama
entities.fact: Panama has coasts on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea, linked by the Panama Canal.

entities.name: Costa Rica
entities.fact: Costa Rica has coasts on both the Pacific Ocean and the Caribbean Sea and protects a large share of its land as national parks.

entities.name: North Korea
entities.fact: North Korea has a Pacific coastline on the Sea of Japan to the east and the Yellow Sea to the west.

entities.name: Taiwan
entities.fact: Taiwan is an island off the coast of China, and its eastern shore faces the open Pacific.

entities.name: Guatemala
entities.fact: Guatemala has a Pacific coast of dark volcanic sand backed by a chain of volcanoes.

entities.name: El Salvador
entities.fact: El Salvador is the only Central American country with no Caribbean coast, so its coastline lies entirely on the Pacific.

entities.name: Nicaragua
entities.fact: Nicaragua has coasts on both the Pacific and the Caribbean, and Lake Nicaragua lies close to its Pacific shore.

entities.name: Malaysia
entities.fact: Malaysia has coasts on the Strait of Malacca and the South China Sea, with the Malaysian part of Borneo facing the Pacific side.

entities.name: Federated States of Micronesia
entities.fact: The Federated States of Micronesia are more than 600 islands scattered across the western Pacific.

entities.name: Brunei
entities.fact: Brunei is a small sultanate on the island of Borneo with a coast on the South China Sea.

entities.name: Niue
entities.fact: Niue is a single raised coral island in the South Pacific and one of the largest of its kind in the world.

entities.name: Honduras
entities.fact: Honduras has a short Pacific coast of about 150 kilometres on the Gulf of Fonseca, though most of its coast faces the Caribbean.

entities.name: India
entities.fact: India has a coastline of more than 7,000 kilometres on the Arabian Sea, the Bay of Bengal and the Indian Ocean itself.

entities.name: Kenya
entities.fact: Kenya's Indian Ocean coast includes the old port of Mombasa and the Swahili town of Lamu.

entities.name: Thailand
entities.fact: Thailand has a west coast on the Andaman Sea, which is part of the Indian Ocean, as well as a coast on the Gulf of Thailand.

entities.name: Tanzania
entities.fact: Tanzania's Indian Ocean coast includes Dar es Salaam and the islands of Zanzibar, Pemba and Mafia.

entities.name: Mozambique
entities.fact: Mozambique has about 2,500 kilometres of Indian Ocean coastline, one of the longest in Africa.

entities.name: Somalia
entities.fact: Somalia has the longest coastline of mainland Africa, about 3,000 kilometres along the Indian Ocean and the Gulf of Aden.

entities.name: Oman
entities.fact: Oman's long coast on the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman includes its capital, Muscat.

entities.name: Yemen
entities.fact: Yemen has coasts on the Red Sea, the Gulf of Aden and the Arabian Sea, and it owns the island of Socotra.

entities.name: Pakistan
entities.fact: Pakistan has an Arabian Sea coast of about 1,000 kilometres, where the port city of Karachi lies.

entities.name: Bangladesh
entities.fact: Bangladesh sits on the Bay of Bengal at the delta of the Ganges, Brahmaputra and Meghna rivers.

entities.name: Myanmar
entities.fact: Myanmar has a long coastline on the Bay of Bengal and the Andaman Sea.

entities.name: Seychelles
entities.fact: The Seychelles are an archipelago of about 115 islands in the western Indian Ocean.

entities.name: Iran
entities.fact: Iran has coasts on the Caspian Sea in the north and on the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman in the south.

entities.name: United Arab Emirates
entities.fact: The United Arab Emirates has coasts on the Persian Gulf and the Gulf of Oman, with Dubai and Abu Dhabi on the Gulf shore.

entities.name: Saudi Arabia
entities.fact: Saudi Arabia has coasts on both the Red Sea and the Persian Gulf.

entities.name: Egypt
entities.fact: Egypt has coasts on both the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, joined by the Suez Canal.

entities.name: Sudan
entities.fact: Sudan's only coast is on the Red Sea, where Port Sudan is its main harbour.

entities.name: Eritrea
entities.fact: Eritrea has a long Red Sea coast that includes the Dahlak Archipelago.

entities.name: Djibouti
entities.fact: Djibouti lies on the Gulf of Aden at the mouth of the Red Sea, beside the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

entities.name: Qatar
entities.fact: Qatar is a peninsula that juts out into the Persian Gulf.

entities.name: Bahrain
entities.fact: Bahrain is an island nation of more than 30 islands in the Persian Gulf.

entities.name: Kuwait
entities.fact: Kuwait lies at the head of the Persian Gulf.

entities.name: Comoros
entities.fact: The Comoros are a volcanic archipelago in the Mozambique Channel between Madagascar and the African mainland.

entities.name: Timor-Leste
entities.fact: Timor-Leste occupies the eastern half of the island of Timor, on the Timor Sea.

entities.name: Singapore
entities.fact: Singapore is an island city-state at the southern tip of the Malay Peninsula beside the Strait of Malacca.

entities.name: Jordan
entities.fact: Jordan's only coast, about 26 kilometres on the Gulf of Aqaba, gives it a port on the Red Sea.

entities.name: Israel
entities.fact: Israel has a Red Sea coast at Eilat as well as a Mediterranean coast.

entities.name: Iraq
entities.fact: Iraq's coast on the Persian Gulf is only about 58 kilometres long, and its main port there is Umm Qasr.

entities.name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
entities.fact: Saint Kitts and Nevis is a twin-island nation and the smallest country in the Americas by area.

entities.name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
entities.fact: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is made up of the volcanic main island of Saint Vincent and a chain of small islands to its south.
